Subject: Follow-up + next steps from today's call (batching & concurrency)

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Product: realtime personalization API (recommendation prompts + short generated copy).
- Traffic: mix of web + background inference; peak spikes during batch scoring windows.
- Technical ask: predictable unit economics and low tail latency for user-affecting calls.

Qualification asks I promised to follow up on (so we can size batching/concurrency):
1) Expected token volume (monthly): range estimate you mentioned on the call.
2) Typical prompt/response lengths (avg input tokens / avg generated tokens).
3) Desired latency SLO for user-facing calls (p50/p95).
4) Any hard budget range or target $/1M tokens you'd like us to aim for.

Early notes on continuous batching assumptions (high level):
- Continuous batching works best when you have a steady stream of small requests rather than purely synchronous single-shot peaks. For mixed workloads we assume: average batch size 8–24, batch timeout ~8–15ms, and a small KV/prefix cache hit rate to avoid rerunning large context.
- Unit economics: continuous batching can reduce per-token GPU time by ~25–45% vs naive single-request serving depending on model and request distribution.

Next steps: can you reply with the 4 items above? I can then share a short cost model (example $/1M tokens based on continuous-batching assumptions) and propose a follow-up technical deep-dive with Aditya to validate latency tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Camila
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila — great summary. Answers below: 

1) Token volume (monthly): we expect an initial rollout at ~50M tokens/month, ramp to ~150–200M tokens/month over the next 6–9 months if latency & cost look good.
2) Average lengths: frontend personalization prompts are small: ~40 tokens input; generation averages ~160 tokens. Background scoring jobs have larger context but are batched off-peak (avg 600 tokens).
3) Latency SLO: user-facing p95 target ~350ms, p50 ~100–120ms. Background scoring is best-effort but we prefer throughput.
4) Budget / target $/1M tokens: procurement asked for target unit economics of $15–$25 / 1M tokens as our planning assumption. Monthly budget range we can tolerate initially: $1k–$6k/month (scalable with committed discounts).

We'll need an outline of expected monthly cost at those unit prices and any specific concurrency limits that would push us into higher tiers. Also please include any assumptions about batching gains (what you measure as continuous-batching uplift).

—Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Platform — FintechCo

Alex — perfect, that's exactly what we needed. Below is a quick, back-of-envelope cost/assumption summary using your numbers so procurement has something to plug into a P&L. I'll follow up with a short spreadsheet (attached) and propose a 30–45m technical deep-dive with Aditya focused on latency SLOs and continuous-batching config.

Assumptions used (continuous batching / routing model):
- Workload mix: 70% user-facing short-gen (40 in / 160 out ≈ 200 tokens per request), 30% background scoring (600 tokens).
- Effective tokens per request (weighted): 0.7*200 + 0.3*600 = 320 tokens avg.
- Steady-state traffic: use your ramp: 50M -> 150–200M tokens/month. We'll model center-case 125M tokens/month for examples.
- Continuous batching improvement: conservatively assume 30% per-token GPU time reduction vs unbatched single-request serving for the front-end mix (numbers vary by model; we can bench with your sample payloads).
- Typical batch settings we recommend to hit your p95 target: max_batch_size 32, batch_timeout 10ms, per-instance concurrency 12–16 (tuned in the deep-dive). These settings aim to maximize batch formation while keeping p95 under 350ms for short-gen flows.

Cost illustrations (simple):
- Target unit price scenarios you provided: $15 / 1M tokens and $25 / 1M tokens.
- For 125M tokens/month: at $15/1M => $1875/mo; at $25/1M => $3125/mo.
- Note: continuous batching can reduce effective GPU consumption; in practice we often achieve additional savings (in GPU-seconds) compared to naive per-request billing, which can make the effective $/1M tokens look lower for heavy short-gen workloads. We'll quantify after a short benchmark.

Risk notes / things that increase cost:
- Very spiky synchronous traffic that prevents batch formation (short spikes produce small batches — higher unit costs).
- Very long generations (>>500 tokens) in the user path without caching will push up compute.
- Large background batch windows are easier to optimize and can be routed to lower-cost capacity.

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached a simple cost_model.xlsx with the numbers above (see FintechCo_cost_model.xlsx).
2) Schedule a 30–45m tech deep-dive with Aditya next week — can you share 2 slots? Aditya will want sample payloads + 1–2 representative prompt sets so we can run a quick onboarding bench.
3) If the bench looks good, we can propose a 3-month pilot with a committed seat/discount to lock unit economics during ramp.

Would you like me to include a sample config (batch_timeout/max_batch_size) per route in the deck we share with procurement?

Thanks,
Camila
